Communication
We are keen to work with parents and carers to provide the best learning experiences for your children. If you have any questions/queries/concerns, please do get in touch. We are happy to help.
Link to ways to get in touch
Please see our vacancies page for more details.
Welcome to High Ham
High Ham Church of England Primary School is first and foremost a school where children are happy, confident and enthusiastic learners. Consistently high standards are expected and achieved. Our Christian ethos is underpinned by the mission statement ‘Discovering, Learning, Believing Together’.
Inspection 2022
We have 6 classes on a stunning rural site with 152 pupils from Reception to Year 6. We are rated as consistently ‘Good’ by Ofsted – Pupils are proud to attend High Ham Primary School. They thrive and feel safe in the caring and nurturing atmosphere.
SIAMS Inspection: Our Statutory Inspection of Anglican and Methodist Schools (SIAMS) took place in September 2024. We are very proud of our report and you are able to read it in full by following the link to our Church page.
“High Ham is a school with Christian love at its core. Lives are transformed by the work of this school.”
Admissions
We welcome applications throughout the year via our online application form. Children starting school for the first time join Reception at the beginning of the academic year in which they turn five.
Applications for Reception places are made through the Somerset County Council admissions form.
For full details on how to apply, please visit our Admissions page.
Wraparound Care
To support our families, we provide high‑quality wraparound care from 7:30am to 5:00pm each school day. This service offers a safe, nurturing environment with a range of activities before and after the school day.
Preschool Provision
We also have an onsite preschool, run by an approved third‑party provider, offering early years provision for younger children. Further information about the preschool, including session availability and admissions, can be found on their dedicated page.

British Values
During the school year we complete a wide range of activities which promote Britsh Values.
Schools are required to promote the spiritual, moral, social and cultural (SMSC) development of their pupils. As part of this, our school actively promotes the fundamental British values of:
All underpinned by equality of opportunity for all.
This is set out in the Department for Education’s guidance on promoting British values in maintained schools
Difference is protected under British law and the Equality Act identifies specific protected characteristics. It is our duty to develop and deepen pupils’ understanding of the fundamental British values. To support equality of opportunity and to promote an inclusive ethos where pupils can thrive together, understanding that difference is a positive, not a negative, and that individual characteristics make a person unique, we use the No Outsiders scheme.
Please click on the link to read the parent/carer guide to the No Outsiders scheme.

How Do Governors Work?
The full Governing Body meets regularly throughout the year—usually six times annually—to review progress, make strategic decisions and monitor school performance.
In addition, there are smaller groups with specific responsibilities:
Business Team
This group oversees the school budget, health and safety, building maintenance, and the wider infrastructure of the school. Although the Business Team is not a formal committee, it reports back to the Full Governing Body with recommendations for approval.
Pay Committee
This committee meets as required to consider staff pay recommendations in line with school policies and national guidance.
Working Groups
These may be set up from time to time to focus on specific areas or projects—for example, policy reviews, building plans or curriculum initiatives.

Relationships, Sex and Health Education (RSHE)
Essential Information:
Sex education at High Ham is not compulsory. Relationships, Health education is mandatory. Our policy which refers to the schemes of work we use has been written in consultation with all stakeholders. Our RSHE policy and associated appendices can be found on the policy/documents page of the website.
Background Information:
As a church school we are part of the Bath and Wells Diocese who have supported our school with how to implement RSHE and to ensure it aligns with our church school ethos.
There is government guidance as well as Church of England and we make use of a range of resources including the ones promoted by the Bath and Wells Diocese (Goodness and Mercy) which has primarily been written for Church of England schools.
We have used the ‘Goodness and Mercy’ knowledge organisers and activity plans to plan our rolling programme which is included in the policy appendices. We use a number of resources to support this programme including the Kapow resources around conception, pregnancy and birth.
Curriculum Overview: We are keen for pupils to understand the spiritual and moral aspects of healthy, loving and nurturing relationships within a context of a Christian vision for the purpose of life. Our overview of the curriculum explains our intent, implementation and impact for this important areas of learning.

Religious Education
Religious Education Curriculum
Religious Education is taught weekly at our school, following the Somerset Agreed Syllabus, Awareness, Mystery and Value. This is further supported by the Understanding Christianity resource materials.
In Key Stage 1, children learn mainly about Christianity and Judaism.In Key Stage 2, pupils explore Christianity, Judaism, Hinduism and Islam.Across both stages, we also introduce children to non‑religious worldviews, such as Humanism, to help them develop a broad understanding of different beliefs and ways of seeing the world.
Parents’ and Carers’ Right to Withdraw from Religious Education (RE)
At High Ham Church of England Primary School, we value the partnership we have with parents and carers in supporting your child’s learning and development. Religious Education (RE) is a vital part of our broad and balanced curriculum, helping pupils to explore and understand different beliefs, cultures, and values in a respectful and inclusive environment.
We understand that some parents may wish to exercise their legal right to withdraw their child from all or part of the RE curriculum. Under the Education Act 1996, parents have the right to withdraw their child from RE lessons if they wish, for reasons of conscience.
If you are considering this option, we encourage you to contact the Headteacher to discuss your concerns and explore how we can best support your child’s educational experience while respecting your wishes. Our aim is always to work collaboratively with families to ensure the best outcomes for every pupil.
Please be aware that withdrawn pupils will be supervised during RE lessons but will not receive alternative teaching unless otherwise arranged.

Young Carers in Schools
Young Carers in Schools
At High Ham C of E Primary School, we recognise the invaluable contributions that young carers make within their families. We understand that some of our pupils may take on additional responsibilities, which can often impact their educational experience.
In our commitment to ensuring that all pupils achieve their best and thrive in our school environment, we are actively working towards achieving the Young Carers in Schools Award. This initiative aims to enhance our support for these pupils, providing them with the necessary resources and understanding to help mitigate the challenges they face.
By fostering an inclusive atmosphere, we aspire to enable young carers to attend and enjoy school alongside their peers, ensuring they have the opportunity to realise their full potential.
How will we achieve this?
What is a Young Carer?
A young carer is someone, under the age of 18, who is caring, unpaid, for a family member or a friend who is ill, disabled, or has a mental health problem or addiction.
They often take on practical and/or emotional caring responsibilities that would normally be expected of an adult. Research suggests there are at least 800,000 young carers in the UK but many do not realise they are a young carer.
We know that young carers may need a little extra support to enjoy and do well at school. We are committed to ensuring that all students who are young carers are identified, and supported effectively.
Please speak to Mrs Edwards or your child’s class teacher if you would like more information regarding young carers at High Ham.

Eco School
In our school we are passionate about the environment and believe we are all responsible for looking after it.
In 2023, ten Key Stage 2 children were elected to become members of the Eco Council. Since then we have been following the Better Planet Schools education project, to support us in reducing our environmental impact.
The Eco Council have lead whole school Collective Worships and offer additional opportunities to all children to engage them in initiatives to reduce waste, increase recycling and improve the biodiversity of our grounds and surrounding areas.

School Communications
We are keen to work with parents and carers to provide the best learning experiences for your children. If you have any questions/queries/concerns, please do get in touch. We are happy to help.
Query about your child:
In the first instance we ask that you contact your child’s class teacher with any queries or concerns. This can be done by emailing the school office or by adding a note in your child’s planner.
Query about general matters:
Please email/phone the school office. Please note we have an answer machine but will get back to you. Emails sent to the school office will be directed to the relevant member of staff. We always aim to get back to you within 48 hours. Please remember staff might be on training and will not always be available.
We have a complaints procedure and guidance which is regularly reviewed by our governors and follows the principles of a graduated response.
Summary of our communication methods:
Pupil planners – these can be used for messages between teacher/parent or carer.
Weekly Class Communication – this the latest source of information and contains dates and reminders for the week ahead. This is emailed to parents and carers every Friday.
Website – hosts all school documents, as well as the diary which can be accessed from the front page of the website.
Class Dojo Story – each class has a class dojo account that parents and carers can join. The class teacher posts regular updates about work and special events happening in class on the class story.
PTA WhatsApp Accounts – these are not organised by the school but by the PTA to share details of PTA events. If you make use of these WhatsApp groups please be mindful that if you want information about school activities, it is always best to contact the class teacher or use the school website online noticeboard/calendar for the most up to date information.
Talk to staff at pick up and drop off times – two members of staff are always at the gate during morning drop-off to welcome the children. You are able to ask any questions/raise any queries at this time. At pick up time, there is an opportunity to speak to the teacher or if collecting from Monkey Madness messages can be passed on.
Phone – our phone line has a 24 hr. answer machine for pupil absence and messages during the school day. If required, someone will get back to you if you leave a message.
School Office – this is open for emails/phone calls between 8:45am and 3:45pm and for in person medical queries/pick ups.
Reporting Absence – Please phone the school office before 9am or report your child’s absence via the attendance email address: attendance@highhamcofe.co.uk
Mental Health and Well-being:
In order to protect the mental health and well-being of the whole school community we respectfully ask you to consider your comments about the school and our staff carefully before posting on any social media platforms. When speaking about your child, please try and do this when your child is not able to overhear your concerns. If appropriate, the teacher will arrange a meeting with both you and your child.

School Council
School Councillors at High Ham Church of England Primary School are committed to improving the school.
At the start of the academic year, potential candidates are invited to stand for election by their peers in a similar way to how members of parliament are elected in Great Britain. This involves the candidates giving speeches and presentations about what they will do as a that will benefit the school.
Once the elections have been completed and candidates have been chosen they are announced to the whole school in one of the weekly assemblies and are presented with the ‘much sought after’ School Councillor badge.
Once elected, School Councillors must maintain an extremely high standard of work as they are role models for the rest of the school.
During 2022 they have been involved in wider school activities including helping the younger pupils at the PTA tuck shop, organising charity donations, running a Mothering Sunday sale as well as supporting a range of activities across the school.
